title: Analysis of covariance
html:
Assume @eq-dsn-ancova-model and @eq-dsn-ancova-rank. Let MW be the orthogonal projection onto C([X,Z]).

  1. MW=M+(I−M)ZEzz−1Z⊤(I−M), and the two terms are orthogonal projections with orthogonal ranges.

  2. 𝛄γ is estimable, with the unique least squares estimate 𝛄γ^=Ezz−1Ezy.

  3. A function 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β is estimable in @eq-dsn-ancova-model iff it is estimable in the model 𝛃E(Y)=Xβ without covariates. If 𝛌𝛒λ=X⊤ρ, its least squares estimate is 𝛌𝛃𝛒𝛄λ⊤β^=ρ⊤M(y−Zγ^),{#eq-dsn-adjusted-estimate}

    so the fitted design part is 𝛃𝛄Xβ^=M(y−Zγ^): the covariance-adjusted response 𝛄y−Zγ^ analysed by the formulas of the model without covariates.

  4. The residual sum of squares is SSE=Eyy−Ezy⊤Ezz−1Ezy,{#eq-dsn-ancova-sse}

    on n−r−q degrees of freedom.

  5. 𝛄Cov(γ^)=σ2Ezz−1, 𝛌𝛃𝛄𝛒Cov(λ⊤β^,γ^)=−σ2ρ⊤MZEzz−1, and 𝛌𝛃𝛒𝛒𝛒𝛒Var(λ⊤β^)=σ2(ρ⊤Mρ+ρ⊤MZEzz−1Z⊤Mρ).{#eq-dsn-ancova-var}

  6. Let C(X0)⊆C(X) with rank r0<r and projection M0, and define Tzz,Tzy,Tyy as in @eq-dsn-within with M0 in place of M. Then @eq-dsn-ancova-rank holds for X0 as well, and the hypothesis that the design part of the mean lies in C(X0), with 𝛄γ unrestricted, has the adjusted sum of squares SSH=(Tyy−Tzy⊤Tzz−1Tzy)−(Eyy−Ezy⊤Ezz−1Ezy){#eq-dsn-adjusted-ss}

    on r−r0 degrees of freedom. If Y is normal, F=SSH/(r−r0)SSE/(n−r−q)∼F(r−r0,n−r−q,γ), where the noncentrality γ, a scalar not to be confused with the coefficient vector 𝛄γ, is given by σ2γ equal to the squared distance from 𝛃𝛄Xβ+Zγ to C([X0,Z]).
